Complete Tutorial

Everything you need to know, from reading basic radar to tracking hurricane hunters in real time.

Overview Menu Layers Alerts Overlays Radio SPC Tropical Models Tools Pro Tips
🗺️
OVERVIEW
Understanding the interface

GWCFC Radar is a live weather map built around a Leaflet map that fills your entire screen. Everything else, controls, legends, overlays, floats on top of the map so the data always takes center stage.

Interface Map
↑ Top-center
GWCFC logo, tap to open the quick menu (Ask AI, Settings, Tutorial, Credits, Sign-in)
← Left sidebar
Layer bubbles, Radar, Satellite, Alerts, Wind, Temp, Waves, Models. Tap any bubble to toggle that layer.
→ Right side
Map tools, style picker, locate, smooth animation toggle, fullscreen, draw, polygon, distance, and radius tools
↘ Bottom-right
Precipitation legend + overlay pill fly-out
↙ Bottom-left
Animation scrubber & playback controls
🔍 Search
Floating search button, jump to any place or feature

There are no mode tabs any more, every data layer lives in one place. Tap a bubble in the left sidebar to switch radar/satellite/alerts/wind on or off, and use the overlay pills (bottom-right) for extras like lightning, weather radio, and surface fronts. The Models bubble opens a single panel that covers both severe and tropical guidance.

The map uses a tile-based system, you can zoom, pan, and rotate freely. Pinch to zoom on mobile, use a three-finger twist gesture to rotate. A compass and ↺ Reset button appear when rotated; tap Reset to snap back to north-up.

💡
First time here? The app opens with current weather alerts and surface fronts already on, for a clean starting view. Tap 📡 Radar in the sidebar to add live NEXRAD, then layer on anything else you need from the bubbles and overlay pills.
☰
QUICK MENU & SEARCH
Tap the logo, everything starts here

Tap the GWCFC logo at the top-center to open the quick menu. This is your home base for the tools that aren't weather layers, the AI assistant, settings, this tutorial, credits, and your account.

🤖
ASK AI

A built-in weather assistant. Ask it plain-English questions, "what does a tornado watch mean?", "is it safe to drive?", "explain CAPE", and it answers using the data on your screen.

⚙️
SETTINGS

Pick your timezone (UTC, local, or any zone), map style (Dark / Light / Satellite / Topo), and toggle coords-on-click, the compass rose, the scale bar, and location tracking.

⭐
CREDITS

Lists every data source and library the radar is built on, NOAA/NWS, Iowa Mesonet, GOES/NESDIS, SPC, NHC, WPC, Broadcastify, Blitzortung, OpenStreetMap, Leaflet, and more.

👤
SIGN IN

Create an account to sync your preferences across devices. Your map style, timezone, and saved settings follow you wherever you open the radar.

🔍 Search Everything

The floating 🔍 search button opens a universal search box. Type a city, ZIP code, or coordinates to fly the map there, or type a feature name ("velocity", "lightning", "HRRR", "hurricane hunters") to jump straight to that layer or tool. Recent searches are remembered for one-tap access.

💡
No tabs needed: Older versions had Regular / Tropical / Severe / Ice tabs across the top. Those are gone, every layer now lives in the left sidebar, and severe + tropical guidance share the single 📊 Models panel. Search is the fastest way to reach anything.
📡
LAYERS
The left sidebar, click any row to toggle

The left sidebar holds floating bubble buttons for each data layer. Tap a bubble to turn it on, it glows cyan when active. Most bubbles open a secondary sub-menu (e.g. tapping Radar lets you choose Reflectivity or Velocity; tapping Satellite lets you choose IR, Visible, or Water Vapor). Note that Radar and Satellite are mutually exclusive, turning one on disables the other.

Actual sidebar bubbles, active bubble glows cyan
📡 Radar LIVE
🛰 Satellite GOES
⚠ Alerts NWS
💨 Wind BARBS
🌡 Temp 2M
🌊 Waves TIDE
📊 Models GFS
📡
RADAR

Tap to choose Reflectivity (precipitation intensity, colored by dBZ), Velocity (wind motion, green toward the radar, red away), or an MRMS product (Multi-Radar Multi-Sensor composite mosaic, 1-hr precip, 24-hr precip, or snow cover). The WSR-88D network updates every 2 minutes; MRMS composites update every 2 minutes as well. Station labels like KTLX (Oklahoma City), KEWX (San Antonio), and KAMX (Miami) appear at close zoom.

🛰
SATELLITE

Tap to choose Infrared, Visible, or Water Vapor imagery, then pick a region (CONUS, Global, Atlantic, Alaska, Hawaii, Full Disk, or Mesoscale). Radar and Satellite are mutually exclusive, enabling one disables the other.

⚠
ALERTS

Opens a sub-menu for WX Alerts (NWS watches, warnings, and advisories drawn as county polygons on the map) and EAS Alerts (live Emergency Alert System broadcasts). Each alert polygon is clickable for the full NWS alert text.

💨
WIND

Opens a sub-menu for Regular wind barbs (sustained 10m wind speed and direction) and Gusts (peak gust barbs). Barbs load instantly using Open-Meteo, a first pass of ~50 barbs appears within ~250ms, then expands to hundreds covering both land and ocean. Arrow points in the wind direction; color scales from blue (calm) through green/yellow to red/purple (severe). Click any barb for speed in mph/kt, direction, and gust info.

🌡
TEMP

Plots 2-meter air temperature markers across the map. Useful for seeing warm/cold sectors, frontal boundaries, and temperature contrasts ahead of and behind storm systems. Each marker shows °F, °C, and the local surface pressure when you click it.

🌊
WAVES

Opens a sub-menu for Tides and Storm Surge. Plots coastal water-level data, great for tracking surge ahead of a landfalling hurricane or checking tide timing along the coast. Click any point for the reading at that location.

📊
MODELS

Opens the unified Models panel covering both Severe guidance (SREF/HREF/NAM/HRRR, SPC Outlooks) and Tropical guidance (spaghetti ensemble tracks, NHC outlooks, GFS/ECMWF/HWRF/HAFS). See the Models section below.

📶
Reading reflectivity colors: Blues and greens are light precipitation (under ~20 mm/hr). Yellow and orange mean moderate to heavy rain. Red (50+ dBZ) indicates heavy rain or large hail. Purple/magenta indicates extreme returns, hail cores or very intense rainfall above 75 mm/hr. On Velocity, green shades move toward the radar, red/orange shades move away, a tight green/red couplet indicates rotation.
Precipitation color scale (mm/h)
LightModerateHeavyIntenseExtreme
🚨
WEATHER ALERTS
Warnings, watches & advisories from NWS

Alerts are overlaid directly on the map as semi-transparent polygons matching the exact county or zone boundaries issued by the National Weather Service. They update in near real-time.

Tornado Warning, most urgent, take shelter immediately
Severe Thunderstorm Warning, damaging wind/hail
Tornado Watch, conditions favorable, stay alert
Severe Thunderstorm Watch, broad area at risk
Flood Warning, flooding occurring or imminent
Mesoscale Discussion, SPC analysis, not yet a watch
⚠️
Warning vs. Watch: A Warning means a hazard is occurring or imminent, take action now. A Watch means conditions are favorable, stay aware and be ready to act.

Each alert polygon on the map is clickable, tap or click it to open a popup with the full NWS alert text, including the affected areas, timing, and hazard details.

⏱ Alert Timeline Bar

Every alert popup now includes a timeline bar at the bottom. It shows the alert's onset time on the left, its expiration on the right, and a colored progress fill marking how far through the alert window you currently are. A status label reads Pending (hasn't started), Active (in effect right now), or Expired, so you can tell at a glance whether a warning is still live and how much time is left on it.

Use the Alerts Panel in the sidebar to see a full list of active alerts sorted by severity. There is also a "past alerts" toggle to review recently expired warnings.

📻 EAS Alerts

The EAS (Emergency Alert System) panel shows active emergency broadcasts from radio stations in your area. These are the same alerts broadcast over the air during severe weather. Each entry shows the station, the alert type, and the broadcast text.

💡
Meso discussions: Toggle the Meso layer to see NWS Mesoscale Discussions, these are issued before a watch is needed and give you 30–90 minutes of lead time on developing severe weather.
🎛️
OVERLAY BAR
Quick-toggle extras, bottom-right corner

Tap the stacked-layers button in the bottom-right corner to fly out the overlay pills. These toggle extra data that complements whatever else you have on, and they stay active no matter what you do with the sidebar layers.

⚡
LIGHTNING

Plots live lightning strike locations as they occur. Each strike appears as a small bolt. Also toggle LTG 30 in the sidebar to show the last 30-minute history with fading intensity.

📻
RADIO STATIONS

Places NOAA Weather Radio transmitter icons on the map. Click any station to see its call sign, frequency, and location, tune in to the live audio stream, and even record it. See the Weather Radio section for the full recording + auto-record feature.

🌥️
FORECAST DOTS

Shows hourly point forecasts as small temperature-colored dot markers across the map. Click any dot to see temperature, wind, precipitation chance, and conditions for that location. Off by default, tap the 🌥️ pill to turn it on.

🛩️
HURRICANE HUNTERS

Tracks NOAA's WP-3D Orion and G-IV aircraft in real time via ADS-B Exchange (free, no key required). Aircraft positions update every 60 seconds. Active recon planes include N42RF "Kermit" and N43RF "Miss Piggy" (WP-3D Orions that penetrate storm eyewalls) and N49RF "Gonzo" (a G-IV that surveys the upper atmosphere around the storm). If no aircraft are airborne, a brief notice appears and clears automatically.

〰️
SURFACE FRONTS

Draws the WPC surface analysis directly on the map, cold fronts (blue), warm fronts (red), stationary and occluded fronts, plus high/low pressure centers. The fastest way to see the boundaries driving today's weather. On by default.

🛩️
Hurricane Hunters: Tap the 🛩️ pill to activate live tracking via ADS-B Exchange, no API key or account needed. NOAA's WP-3D Orions (N42RF "Kermit", N43RF "Miss Piggy") and G-IV jet (N49RF "Gonzo") appear as plane icons when airborne. Click any aircraft for its call sign, altitude, speed, and heading. During Hurricane Milton (Oct 2024), Kermit flew through the eyewall at 1,500 ft while the storm was Cat 5, visible in real time on this layer. If no aircraft are airborne, a brief notice appears and clears automatically.
📻
WEATHER RADIO & RECORDING
Listen to NOAA Weather Radio, and record alerts automatically

Tap the 📻 Radio overlay pill to drop NOAA Weather Radio (NWR) transmitter icons onto the map. NWR is the government network of stations that broadcast continuous weather and emergency information on 162.400–162.550 MHz. Click any station icon to open its panel.

🔊
LIVE AUDIO

Each station popup streams the live broadcast right in your browser, the same robotic NWR voice you'd hear on a physical weather radio. It pulls from several public stream networks and falls back automatically if one is down.

🔴
RECORD

Hit 🔴 Rec in any station popup to capture the live audio. Recordings are saved locally and can be downloaded as MP3, WebM, Opus, FLAC, or AAC. Perfect for grabbing the exact wording of a warning as it's read on-air.

⚡
AUTO-RECORD

Arm AUTO and the radar will automatically start recording the nearest station whenever a qualifying NWS warning fires, no need to be watching. Set how many minutes each capture should run, and it stops and saves on its own.

💾
ARCHIVE

Every recording is stored in an on-device archive (it survives page reloads). The panel shows each clip's station, length, and timestamp, with inline playback, per-clip download, and delete, plus a "Clear all" to wipe the archive.

Setting up Auto-Record

1
Tap the 📻 Radio pill so the station markers and the recordings panel are loaded.
2
Press the AUTO button. It turns red (🔴 AUTO) and the panel shows an ⚡ ARMED status bar.
3
In the "Stop after" box, type how many minutes each automatic recording should last (1–120).
4
Leave it armed. When a warning hits, the radar finds the closest NWR transmitter, records it for your chosen length, and files the clip in the archive automatically.
💡
Why record NWR? The on-air wording often contains detail (exact impact statements, "tornado emergency" language, evacuation instructions) that's worth keeping. Auto-record means you capture it even if you weren't at the screen when the warning was issued.
📡
Heads up: Live streams come from third-party relays and can occasionally drop or be region-blocked. If a station won't play, try another nearby transmitter, and remember this is a convenience tool, not a substitute for a real NOAA Weather Radio receiver during emergencies.
⚠️
SPC OUTLOOKS
Models panel → Severe, Storm Prediction Center risk areas

Open the 📊 Models bubble in the sidebar and select the Severe pill, then turn on SPC Outlooks. SPC issues categorical and probabilistic outlooks for Days 1, 2, and 3, indicating where conditions favor severe thunderstorms.

General, general thunderstorms possible; no organized severe weather expected
Slight (SLGT), scattered severe storms likely; well-organized activity possible
Enhanced (ENH), numerous severe storms expected
Moderate (MDT), significant severe weather outbreak likely
High (HIGH), particularly dangerous situation (PDS), rare

Switch between Day 1, Day 2, and Day 3 inside the panel. Day 1 is the current day's outlook (updated several times daily); Day 2 covers tomorrow; Day 3 covers the day after.

⚠️
Moderate or High Risk? These are rare events, issued only when SPC is highly confident in a widespread severe weather outbreak. A High risk day means a particularly dangerous situation (PDS) is expected. Notable historic High Risk days include April 27, 2011 (the 2011 Super Outbreak, 211 tornadoes in one day, including the EF5 that struck Tuscaloosa and Birmingham, AL) and May 20, 2013 (EF5 Moore, OK tornado, 1.3-mile-wide, 210 mph winds).
🌀
TROPICAL MODE
Hurricane tracking & tropical analysis

Open the 📊 Models bubble and select the Tropical pill during hurricane season (June 1 – November 30). The panel loads tropical track guidance, ensemble spaghetti plots, and NHC products. Recent major storms tracked here include Hurricane Milton (Cat 5, Oct 2024, rapidly intensified to 180 mph before striking Florida's Gulf Coast near Siesta Key) and Hurricane Helene (Cat 4, Sep 2024, made landfall near Perry, FL and caused catastrophic inland flooding through the Southern Appalachians).

🌀
NHC FORECAST CONE

The official 5-day track forecast from the National Hurricane Center. The cone shows the probable path of the storm's center. Approximately 2/3 of historical storms stay within the cone, but impacts extend well outside it.

🔵
INVEST AREAS

Disturbances being monitored for development. Numbered 90L–99L (Atlantic) or 90E–99E (East Pacific). For example, Invest 97L in August 2024 eventually became Hurricane Helene. When an invest reaches watch/warning criteria, NHC issues advisories and may name the system.

🌡️
SEA SURFACE TEMP

Critical fuel for tropical systems. Warm water above 26°C (79°F) to a depth of at least 50 meters is generally required to sustain a hurricane. The SST layer uses NOAA's Coral Reef Watch composite.

📊
TROPICAL MODELS

A Tropical Tidbits-style model viewer inside the map. Available models: GFS, ECMWF (Euro), GEFS-Avg, CMC (Canadian), ICON (German), NAM, HWRF, HAFS-A, and HAFS-B. Pick a region and parameter, then step through hours or hit Play.

🛩️
Combine Tropical + Hurricane Hunters: While in Tropical mode, activate the 🛩️ Hurricane Hunters overlay to see NOAA's recon aircraft flying into the storm in real time. Their data feeds directly into NHC's intensity analysis.

Using the Tropical Model Viewer

1
Tap the 📊 Models bubble in the sidebar, then select the Tropical pill. The model viewer slides in.
2
Choose your Model (GFS, ECMWF, GEFS-Avg, CMC, ICON, NAM, HWRF, HAFS-A, HAFS-B) and Region (Atlantic Basin, W. Atlantic/US East, E. Pacific, C. Pacific, W. Pacific, S. Hemisphere, Indian Ocean, or Global).
3
Select a Parameter: MSLP + 6h Precip, 500mb Vort + Heights, 200mb Wind (Jet Stream), 850mb Wind, 2m Temperature, Total Precip, or Precipitable Water.
4
Pick a Run (model initialization time) and use the frame slider or ▶ Play to animate the forecast.
🖥️
WEATHER MODELS
GFS, NAM, HRRR, SREF, HREF & more

The 📊 Models bubble is always available in the sidebar. Tapping it opens a single panel with a Severe ⟷ Tropical pill switch at the top, Severe for convective/short-range guidance, Tropical for hurricane track models. A floating info box on the map shows which run is loaded, the resolution, the variable, and current forecast hour.

ModelGFS · NOAA
Run12Z · May 8, 2026
Resolution0.25° (~28 km)
VariableTotal Precip (mm)
Forecast HourF+024h (valid May 9, 12Z)

For severe weather model guidance, choose the Severe pill in the Models panel. It gives you:

🔢
SREF

Short-Range Ensemble Forecast, a multi-model ensemble highlighting forecast uncertainty in the 0–84 hour range. Useful for identifying where confidence is high versus where solutions diverge. (The legacy SREF was replaced by NCEP's Rapid Ensemble Forecast System in 2021; some platforms still display it as SREF.)

🔢
HREF

High-Resolution Ensemble Forecast, combines HRRR, NAM, and other hi-res models. Excellent for convective initiation timing and QPF (precipitation amount) within 48 hours.

🔢
NAM

North American Mesoscale model, 3km nest available. Standard go-to for mesoscale features, frontal positions, and short-range QPF. Updated 4x daily.

🔢
HRRR

High-Resolution Rapid Refresh, 3km, updated hourly. The gold standard for convective forecasting within 18 hours. Variables include QPF, CAPE, shear, soundings, and hodographs.

Within the Severe model panel you can switch parameters: QPF (precipitation), CAPE (instability), Shear (wind shear), 500mb heights, Hodo (hodograph / storm motion), SRH (storm-relative helicity), and Sounding. Use the run selector and hour slider to step through the forecast.

🛠️
MAP TOOLS
Drawing, animation, compass & more
✏️
DRAW

Opens a floating toolbar. Pick a color from the palette and draw freehand annotations directly on the map. Supports undo/redo. Export your annotated map as a PNG image.

⬡
POLYGON

Draw a closed polygon on the map by clicking to place vertices, then clicking the first point to close it. The finished polygon area shows its square mileage. Great for outlining a county, metro area, or any custom region of interest.

📏
DISTANCE

Click two or more points on the map to measure straight-line distances. Each segment shows its length in miles and kilometers, and the running total updates as you add points. Double-click to finish. Great for estimating how far a storm is from a city or how wide a tornado path is.

◎
RADIUS RINGS

Click the map to drop a center point, then drag to set the radius. The ring shows its radius in miles. Useful for "how close is this storm to my town?" or checking if a storm is within a certain distance of a populated area.

〰️
TRACK MAKER

Plot a custom storm track by clicking waypoints. The path connects them in order and can be exported as a PNG. Useful for sketching expected storm paths or comparing against official NHC cone guidance.

▶️
ANIMATION BAR

The bottom bar scrubs through recent radar or satellite frames. Hit Play to loop, adjust speed with the input, or step frame-by-frame. Great for tracking storm motion and estimating where cells will be in 15–30 minutes.

🧭
COMPASS & ROTATION

Use a three-finger rotate gesture on mobile to rotate the map. A compass appears showing your current bearing, and a ↺ Reset button appears, tap it to snap back to north-up.

🗺️
MAP STYLES

Four base map styles available: 🌑 Dark (default, best for radar contrast), 🛰 Satellite (aerial imagery), 🌤 Light (clean minimal), and 🗺 Topo (terrain with elevation). Switch styles from the right-side bubble menu or via ⚙ Settings → Map Style. The right-side menu also has 📍 Locate (center on your GPS position), ✨ Smooth animation toggle, and ⛶ Fullscreen.

Animating Radar

1
Make sure the Radar or Satellite bubble is active in the sidebar.
2
The animation bar at the bottom of the screen shows loaded frames. Each tick is one time step.
3
Press ▶ Play to loop the animation. Use the slider to jump to a specific frame.
4
Watch storm cells move across the map, note direction and speed to estimate where they'll be in 15–30 minutes.
🏆
PRO TIPS
Getting the most out of every feature
🌀 + 🛩️
RECON + NHC COMBO

During active storms: open 📊 Models → Tropical for the NHC track guidance, then activate the 🛩️ Hurricane Hunters overlay pill. Watch N42RF "Kermit" fly through the eyewall in real time while the track guidance updates in the background.

📻 + ⚡
SET-AND-FORGET RECORDING

Before severe weather arrives, tap the 📻 Radio pill, press AUTO, and set a duration. The radar will record the on-air warning from the nearest NWR transmitter the instant it's issued, even if you've stepped away from the screen.

⚡
LIVE LIGHTNING

Real-time lightning strikes from the Blitzortung community network. Each bolt appears on the map within seconds of occurring. Toggle the ⚡ pill at any time, works across all modes.

🌧️
MRMS PRODUCTS

Under the 📡 Radar bubble, tap MRMS Mosaic for a seamless national composite that fills gaps between single-site radars. Add 1-hr or 24-hr Precip to see rainfall accumulation totals, or Snow Cover during winter events. Multiple MRMS layers can be active at the same time.

⚠ + 📊
SPC + HRRR

Cross-reference the SPC Day 1 outlook area with HRRR CAPE and shear fields. If the HRRR shows 2000+ J/kg CAPE and 40+ kts of bulk shear inside a Moderate risk, that's a serious setup.

🌥️
FORECAST DOTS

Click multiple forecast dots along a storm's projected path to quickly compare conditions, temperature, humidity, wind, ahead of the storm versus behind it.

🌊
SST FOR INTENSITY

Before a hurricane makes landfall, overlay SST. Warm eddies (Loop Current, Gulf Stream) often cause rapid intensification. Cold upwelling from a slow-moving storm can weaken it.

📱
Mobile use: The map is fully touch-optimized. Pinch to zoom, single-finger pan, two-finger rotate. Overlay pills and tabs are sized for thumb-friendly tapping. In landscape mode you get more map real estate.
🚨
Safety first: This radar is a situational awareness tool. It does not replace official NWS warnings delivered through NOAA Weather Radio, Wireless Emergency Alerts, or local emergency management. Always follow local shelter instructions during active warnings.
